response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT college_id, COUNT(DISTINCT player_id) AS cnt FROM player_college GROUP BY college_id), s AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total FROM c) SELECT AVG(c.cnt * 1.0) AS avg_count_above, AVG(c.cnt * 1.0 / s.total) AS avg_share_of_total, AVG(c.cnt - s.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM c CROSS JOIN s WHERE c.cnt > s.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: Records with NULL college_id form one group (GROUP BY puts NULLs together). The group is counted as a college in the all-college average and the total.
The total of counts is the sum of per-college distinct-player counts. A player who attended several colleges is counted once in each, so this total can exceed the number of distinct players.
Rows with NULL player_id are not counted, because COUNT(DISTINCT) ignores NULLs.
